historical_references.context: Mustazhir Billah was the title of the Abbasid caliphs who ruled from the city of Baghdad. The title is an Arabic phrase meaning 'Protector of the Throne' or 'The Settler on the Throne'. The caliphs used this title to indicate their position as the rightful rulers of the Islamic world and their duty to protect and preserve the Islamic faith.

historical_references.context: Mustazhir Billah was the last Abbasid caliph of Baghdad, who reigned during the Mongol invasion of the Middle East. After the Mongols conquered Baghdad, Mustazhir was captured and taken to the Mongol court. There he was treated with respect and given a position of authority. He continued to rule as a figurehead caliph, but the real power was in the hands of the Mongol rulers.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Mustazhir' is derived from the Arabic word 'istazhara', which means 'to reside' or 'to dwell'. In the context of Islamic finance, a Mustazhir is an individual who is considered an owner of an asset but does not possess it physically. This concept is crucial in the Islamic mortgage system, where the borrower does not own the property until all installments have been paid. The Mustazhir is thus a tenant, with the right to reside in the property and use it as collateral for the loan. This concept is gaining popularity in the modern Islamic finance industry, and is seen on platforms such as ZakatWise app, Meezan Bank, and the Islamic Real Estate Fund. The trend towards Mustazhir arrangements is driven by the growing interest in Shariah-compliant finance and the need for flexible, long-term investment options. Additionally, the focus on sustainable living and ethical investment is increasing the demand for Mustazhir arrangements in real estate, as they offer a way to invest in property while avoiding the moral and environmental issues associated with ownership.
